name: Josh Shapiro
background: Governor since 2023; age 53; Montgomery County. Served three terms in the state House and six years as attorney general. Running mate: Lt. Gov. Austin Davis.
platform: Abortion access; legalizing recreational marijuana; an 'all of the above' energy approach including solar, wind, oil and gas; tighter data center standards; public school funding and economic development; LGBTQ rights.
money: Raised tens of millions and had over 34 times Garrity's cash on hand in June. Top donors include Michael Bloomberg, IBEW Local 98's committee, Greater PA Carpenters PAC, Democracy PAC II (started by George Soros) and Christian Larsen. Put $10 million of campaign money into flipping congressional seats and the state Senate.
notes: Senate Republicans blocked his minimum wage, gun and LGBTQ nondiscrimination priorities; budgets passed late; critics cite his executive orders and a shifting data center stance. Often mentioned as a possible 2028 presidential candidate.

name: Stacy Garrity

platform: Pro-life with exceptions for rape, incest and the life of the mother; opposes recreational marijuana; a special session on energy costs, lower utility taxes and more natural gas production; a pause on data centers.
money: Raised almost $5.4 million Sept. 15 to Oct. 19, much tied to the skill games industry. Top donors include University City Housing Co. (Michael Karp), Keystone Honor PAC, Bob Asher and PA Future Fund, and skill games founder Michael Pace.
notes: Questioned 2020 election results at a 2022 rally. Drew scrutiny for a $45 million Israel Bonds purchase, a $500 million loan program during the 2025 budget impasse (she denies it was political) and a reported $33,500 flight from Pace.

platform: Privatize schools; end school property taxes; phase out the state income tax; end mail ballots; expand voter ID; decriminalize drugs.
notes: The only third-party candidate on the November ballot.

endorsements: EMILY's List, Planned Parenthood Action PAC, American Federation of Teachers, Philadelphia Federation of Teachers, League of Conservation Voters, Sierra Club and Bucks County Democrats, among others.
money: Backed by the Senate Democratic campaign committee, which spent about $12 million on Republican-held seats June 8 to Oct. 19 (no per-race figure published).
notes: Farry's lawyer sent her campaign a cease-and-desist letter calling her 'data senator' ad defamatory. She pressed Farry to drop his co-sponsorship of SB 933, which would expand automated license plate readers.

Supports annual minimum wage increases, a youth activities tax credit, open primaries and long-term SEPTA funding, though he voted against a House SEPTA bill in 2025.
